events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
Two preliminary points settle the shape of this case. First, the ride is a fixed-fare RydeX trip: the rider was charged a quoted $25.04 made up of base $3.90 + distance $15.17 (10.8 km) + time $4.50 + platform $1.47, with waiting $0.00 and no discount [F6], and the billed distance does not exceed the optimal route (10.8 km vs 10.8 km) [F4]. Second, on the metered branch the trace's RD-2 screen fails: RydeX is a fixed-fare service, so extra kilometres do not enter the fare [F6][RD-2][RD-1]. The rider's demand to be "refunded the extra distance" therefore has no monetary object on this service; the only refundable items would be an unpublished or unsupported post-trip add-on [F6][FARE-1], and none appears in the fare breakdown.

The trip was nonetheless driven off the optimal route. There is one off-route segment, 14:19–14:22, 2.15 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.38 km, adding 0.77 km [F3]; total actual distance was 12.4 km against 10.8 km optimal (+1.6 km) and duration 18.9 min against 17 min [F1][F2]. That segment is a route deviation within RD-1, which sets no percentage or absolute-km threshold: the driver's duty is the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and any unexplained deviation breaches it [F3][RD-1].

No exemption applies. The driver's "reasonable cause" claim is that his GPS rerouted him [F8], but RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the detour began; the record shows no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F11], and the two speed-band facts are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on roads that are not tied to the replaced stretch at band 1–2 [F9][F10][F3][RD-4]. Speed-band evidence alone does not exempt a segment, so the segment stands unexcused under RD-4. [F3][F9][F10][F11][RD-4]

Nor did the rider consent. The in-app chat contains no messages at all between rider and driver [F7], so there is no rider message naming a road, area or route that could tie itself to the 14:19–14:22 segment, and no rider-named stop in that segment [F3][F7][RD-5][RD-3]. The only assertion of agreement is the driver's post-trip statement that he followed his GPS and that the fare is fine [F8] — a driver's own claim of acquiescence is not the rider's prior consent, and the chat record here is complete and empty, so the finding is that the segment counts, not that it is undetermined [F7][F8][RD-5][RD-3]. Because the segment is not exempt, RD-1 is recorded as breached against the driver. [F3][RD-1]

The consequence is not money. RD-2's metered branch (extra_km × per-km rate) is unavailable because this is a fixed-fare RydeX trip in which mileage changes do not alter the charge: the billed distance equals the optimal distance and the fare is a quotation [F4][F6][RD-2]. The refundable amount is therefore $0.00, and the only remaining refundable item would be an undisclosed or unsupported surcharge, of which the breakdown shows none [F6][FARE-1]. With a nil refund, the outcome on the money is no_action together with the recorded RD-1 breach [F4][F6][RD-2]. Confidence is high on the conclusions (fixed fare; empty chat; no qualifying incident) and lower only on the geometric attribution of the segment. [F1][F3][F6][F11]

The established breach does trigger an account action. RD-6 applies where the case is made out against the driver and the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F14], so this second upheld case makes it repeated and the ruling carries flag_account. The rider's own profile (2 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) is irrelevant to liability either way and does not decide anything here. [F13][F14][RD-6]

Safety screen: the complaint, the single driver statement and the (empty) chat contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8]; the rider's complaint is confined to route and fare [F7]. SAFE-1 is checked and nothing is flagged. [F7][F8][SAFE-1]

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked into your ride and reviewed the fare. Your trip was a fixed-price ride, so the price you were quoted is what applies — extra distance on the road doesn't change it. Because of that, there's nothing to refund, so we're not issuing a refund.

We did find that the driver went off the best route for part of the trip without a good reason, and we've recorded that on the driver's account. This is the driver's second upheld route issue recently, so their account is being sent for review.

Your account isn't affected. If you have questions, reply in the app.

DRIVER: We reviewed the rider's dispute about this trip. The fare was correct — fixed-price trip, no refund owed — so no refund will be paid (amount: $0.00).

However, we found one part of the trip where you drove off the shortest and most direct route without a valid reason. Your GPS excuse didn't qualify: there was no traffic incident on the route you should have taken, and no message from the rider agreeing to a different way.

Because you already have an upheld route deviation in the last 90 days, this second one counts as repeated. It's being recorded on your account and your account is being sent to Ryde review. No money is taken from you for this.

That segment is a route deviation within RD-1, which sets no percentage or absolute-km threshold: the driver's duty is the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and any unexplained deviation breaches it [F3][RD-1].

No exemption applies. The driver's "reasonable cause" claim is that his GPS rerouted him [F8], but RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the detour began; the record shows no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F11], and the two speed-band facts are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on roads that are not tied to the replaced stretch at band 1–2 [F9][F10][F3][RD-4]. Speed-band evidence alone does not exempt a segment, so the segment stands unexcused under RD-4. [F3][F9][F10][F11][RD-4]

Nor did the rider consent. The in-app chat contains no messages at all between rider and driver [F7], so there is no rider message naming a road, area or route that could tie itself to the 14:19–14:22 segment, and no rider-named stop in that segment [F3][F7][RD-5][RD-3]. The only assertion of agreement is the driver's post-trip statement that he followed his GPS and that the fare is fine [F8] — a driver's own claim of acquiescence is not the rider's prior consent, and the chat record here is complete and empty, so the finding is that the segment counts, not that it is undetermined [F7][F8][RD-5][RD-3]. Because the segment is not exempt, RD-1 is recorded as breached against the driver. [F3][RD-1]

The consequence is not money. RD-2's metered branch (extra_km × per-km rate) is unavailable because this is a fixed-fare RydeX trip in which mileage changes do not alter the charge: the billed distance equals the optimal distance and the fare is a quotation [F4][F6][RD-2]. The refundable amount is therefore $0.00, and the only remaining refundable item would be an undisclosed or unsupported surcharge, of which the breakdown shows none [F6][FARE-1]. With a nil refund, the outcome on the money is no_action together with the recorded RD-1 breach [F4][F6][RD-2]. Confidence is high on the conclusions (fixed fare; empty chat; no qualifying incident) and lower only on the geometric attribution of the segment. [F1][F3][F6][F11]

The established breach does trigger an account action. RD-6 applies where the case is made out against the driver and the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F14], so this second upheld case makes it repeated and the ruling carries flag_account. The rider's own profile (2 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) is irrelevant to liability either way and does not decide anything here. [F13][F14][RD-6]

Safety screen: the complaint, the single driver statement and the (empty) chat contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8]; the rider's complaint is confined to route and fare [F7]. SAFE-1 is checked and nothing is flagged. [F7][F8][SAFE-1]

The driver's assertion that he merely followed his GPS and that nothing is wrong with the fare does not excuse the segment: RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, and none is recorded during the trip window [F8][F11][F3][RD-4]; the unexempted segment stands as an RD-1 breach even though the fixed fare makes the refundable amount zero [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 14:19–14:22 (2.15 km vs 1.38 km optimal, +0.77 km) [F3]. No exemption under RD-5: the in-app chat contains no messages between rider and driver, so no rider message sent before 14:19:15 names a road/area/route the driver proposed [F7]; the driver's post-trip statement that he followed his GPS is a claim of agreement, not the rider's prior consent, and the chat record is complete, so the finding is counts rather than undetermined [F8][RD-5]. No exemption under RD-3: this segment contains no measured rider-requested stop and no rider message naming a place [F3][F7][RD-3]. No exemption under RD-4: no traffic incident on the replaced stretch before the detour, and the band-4 speed records are neither on the replaced stretch at band 1–2 nor sufficient alone [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. The segment is therefore an unexcused deviation under RD-1 [F3][RD-1]; because the trip is fixed-fare the extra kilometres generate no refundable amount [F4][F6][RD-2].

notices.text:
We looked into your ride and reviewed the fare. Your trip was a fixed-price ride, so the price you were quoted is what applies — extra distance on the road doesn't change it. Because of that, there's nothing to refund, so we're not issuing a refund.

We did find that the driver went off the best route for part of the trip without a good reason, and we've recorded that on the driver's account. This is the driver's second upheld route issue recently, so their account is being sent for review.

Your account isn't affected. If you have questions, reply in the app.

We reviewed the rider's dispute about this trip. The fare was correct — fixed-price trip, no refund owed — so no refund will be paid (amount: $0.00).

However, we found one part of the trip where you drove off the shortest and most direct route without a valid reason. Your GPS excuse didn't qualify: there was no traffic incident on the route you should have taken, and no message from the rider agreeing to a different way.

Because you already have an upheld route deviation in the last 90 days, this second one counts as repeated. It's being recorded on your account and your account is being sent to Ryde review. No money is taken from you for this.
